correctness.rationale: For every odd p and d>=2, the group, left and right skew-brace and swapped lambda identities are explicitly derived; simultaneous preservation of the two laws is shown equivalent to conjugacy of omega-selfadjoint operators. The hyperbolic cyclic-pair decomposition proves the critical symplectic normal form, and the rational-canonical Euler product counts its classes. Nondegeneracy is equivalent to T invertible. The local standalone verifier exhausted all 729 alternating beta over F3^4 and independently checked all brace lambda identities at d=1,p=3. Finite tests are supplementary, not infinite proofs; the theorem excludes noncentral/nonbilinear additions.

originality.rationale: The established forward/inverse Baer constructions do not alone identify isomorphism orbits. Waterhouse already supplies the matrix symplectic normal form and rational canonical counts are classical; both are credited. The remaining synthesis—explicit fixed Heisenberg brace fiber, equivalence of brace isomorphism to symplectic conjugacy, and exact nonabelian-additive orbit count—is not implied by the identified prior statements and did not match accessible indexed records. Important residual risk is inability to read full text of the September 2026 inverse-deformation preprint; PASS is provisional self-review, not proof of global novelty.

value.rationale: A new forward/inverse Baer mechanism makes noninjective fibers a motivated classification question. The result identifies the exact isomorphism types of the entire natural central-bilinear family over each fixed high-rank extraspecial Heisenberg multiplicative group, including a sharp count where both laws define extraspecial groups. The group-law-to-symplectic-conjugacy bridge is structurally nontrivial, and numbers p^2+p and p^2-1 already distinguish meaningful types beyond order-p^3; the work does not claim generic matrix class enumeration itself is new.
